question: Relaxing the exact-target demand (a == N) to ANY tree node with gcd(a,N) > 1: how much does expected hitting time drop, and does B1 enter a new scaling class?

prestated.E1: B1 collapses toward B3/B4 behavior; slope < 0.6 would be NEW and major; reference bands TD 0.84-1.14, rho ~0.52

part_a_multitarget_census.concentration_verdict: HITS-AT-FIRST-CROSSING: median(hit depth - minimal crossing depth) = 6.0; 0.0% of hits land within depth +1 of where values first reach min(p,q) scale.

B2_blind_exact_aN_analytic.note: analytic FIFO visits (3^(dB+1)-1)/2 x4 units; infeasible to simulate

part_b_B1_equivalence_verdict: HYBRID / BUDGET-DOMINATED-WITH-MEASURABLE-TAIL: 55% of Ns censored at budget, but the finished 682 Ns span log2s [11.004, 14.746] and give alpha=1.169 (r2=0.7926) -- NOT below 0.6, so the pre-stated NEW-and-major sub-linear regime is REFUTED; where it finishes at all, multi-target FIFO behaves like trial division or worse. Slope fitted on the FINISHED subset only -- that subset is size-biased toward smaller min(p,q) (hits need a >= min(p,q) to exist and depth-ordered BFS reaches large a late), so treat alpha as indicative, not a clean scaling law. Value-ordered expansion (part c) finishes 100% of Ns with alpha=1.087: the relaxation pays off ONLY under value ordering, and then lands in the trial-division class.

part_c_energy_guidance.priority: dist(a, nearest multiple of N), best-first, cap 4N, same budget
part_c_energy_guidance.verdict: GUIDANCE-HELPS: z=38.73 (FIFO wins 0, guided wins 1500, ties 0), median paired ratio 0.1109318843770785 -- AGAINST the pre-stated magnitude-mirror-seal expectation, stated plainly. Mechanism (from data): guided first-hits land at small multiples of min(p,q) (median hit_a/min(p,q) = 1.00, 100.0% of them at a < N, 100.0% exactly at a = min(p,q)); the priority dist(a,N)=min(a mod N, N-a mod N) is monotone increasing in a on [0, N/2], so best-first DEGENERATES TO AN ASCENDING-VALUE SWEEP over the tree's dense value set until it enters divisibility territory (a >= min(p,q)). The guidance sweeps VALUES toward multiples of the prime factors; it does not sense modular structure.

ledger: PRICING: 1 visit = 4 units (1 mul + 1 gcd@3); child-value arithmetic excluded uniformly from B1/B2/guided; TD division := 1 unit (x3 shifts constants only, not slopes); rho iter := 1, gcd batch := 3, failed restarts counted.
B2 is ANALYTIC: visits = (3^(dB+1)-1)//2 from the exact unique parent-climb depth dB (median 34, range 13..4580); simulating is computationally impossible at median dB.
K4 walk REUSED the K1 walk on 32.0% of Ns (rule: K1 budget-bound AND zero cap-prunes => identical FIFO prefix); K4-minus-K1 total hits = 47.
Value cap binding within the 200000-node budget: K4 walk cap-pruned >0 nodes on 374/1500 Ns (202725 prunes total).
B1 censored (no hit within budget) on 818/1500 Ns; slope fitted on uncensored only.

LEDGER CATCH: FIFO first-hit times exceed the uniform-modular-random prediction E~pq/(p+q); the median gap is 3.744 log2 units (see part_b_B1_theory_gap_log2) -- tree values are NOT uniform mod p at fixed depth (small-a nodes overrepresented), so 'multiple targets = modular luck' FAILS as a model of depth-ordered search; it holds only for value-ordered search, where hits arrive exactly AT a=min(p,q).
Guidance overhead (heap push/pop) excluded from the matched-compute unit count; mean/max heap watermark 42546/83723 entries.
NOTE s-range: min(p,q) in [11.00,15.00] log2 -- q's lower bound (2^13) exceeds p's floor, so s spans [2^11+1, 2^15-1] regardless of q.
